samples.text:
The diagram shows the process of recycling the used glass bottles. There are eight stages in this process.

Firstly, people leave their empty bottles in bottle banks in the street. Then a lorry take the bottles to the recycling plant. After that, the bottles are sorted by colour, so clear, green and brown glass are separated. Next, the labels and caps are removed and the bottles is washed with high-pressure water.

In the fifth stage, the glass is crushed into small pieces, which are called cullet. Then the cullet is mix with sand and heated to 1,500°C. After this, the molten glass is shaped to new bottles in the moulding stage. Finally, the new bottles are sent to drinks factories and shops.

Overall, the process starts with the collection of bottles and ends with the distribution of new bottles, and then it begin again from the collection stage, so it is a cycle. The most important part is at the recycling plant where the glass is sorted, cleaned, crushed and melted.
samples.why: Overview present but placed at the end · all stages covered in order · mechanical linking (Firstly, Then, After that) · adequate vocabulary · several agreement and preposition errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the way in which used glass bottles are recycled so that they can be turned into new ones.

Overall, the process is cyclical and consists of eight stages, beginning with the collection of empty bottles from street bottle banks and ending with the distribution of new bottles, after which the cycle starts again.

To begin with, bottles are left by the public in bottle banks, from where they are taken by lorry to a recycling plant. At the plant, they are sorted according to colour into clear, green and brown glass. The sorted bottles are then cleaned, labels and caps are removed and the glass is washed with high-pressure water.

In the next stage, the glass is crushed into a small pieces known as cullet. This cullet is mixed with sand and heated to a temperature of 1,500°C, and the resulting molten glass is shaped into new bottles in moulds. Finally, these bottles are sent to drinks factories and shops, and the whole process then begins again with the collection stage, meaning that the same glass can be used many times.
samples.why: Clear overview stating the cycle and eight stages · logical progression with passive forms · good range of linking · some less common vocabulary · mostly accurate with two minor slips.

samples.text:
The diagram depicts the stages through which discarded glass bottles pass as they are recycled into new containers.

It is clear that this is a continuous, eight-stage cycle. It begins when empty bottles are deposited in street bottle banks and concludes with newly manufactured bottles being dispatched to retailers, at which point the sequence starts afresh.

Once the bottles have been collected from bottle banks, they are transported by lorry to a recycling plant, where they are sorted into clear, green and brown glass. Each batch is subsequently cleaned, with labels and caps being stripped off before the glass is washed using high-pressure water.

The clean glass is then crushed into small fragments, referred to as cullet. In the melting phase, this cullet is combined with sand and heated to 1,500°C, producing molten glass that is moulded into fresh bottles. In the final stage, the finished bottles are distributed to drinks factories and shops. From there, the bottles eventually find their way back to street bottle banks, completing the loop and allowing the same glass to be reused repeatedly.
samples.why: Well-placed overview identifying the cycle and its end points · every stage skilfully sequenced · precise vocabulary (deposited, dispatched, cullet) · wide range of passive and participle structures · error-free.
